newsitem.title: UK: Funds at Jardine Fleming down 10 pct - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Funds at Jardine Fleming down 10 pct - newspaper.

text.p: Funds under management at Jardine Fleming Investment Management (JFIM) have fallen 10 percent in the past six months, with British business among the worst affected, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.
JFIM chief operating officer Mark White said in the FT report that funds under management stood at $20 billion, down from $22 billion at the end of the first half of last year.

"Obviously there has been some fallout from the combination of the regulatory difficulties that we had last year and the fact that Asian markets have failed to perform as well as Western markets for the third consecutive year," White was quoted as saying.

"The UK was clearly the market that was most affected at the practical level," White said in the report. The newspaper said Britain's Post Office Superannuation Scheme and Avon County Council were among the biggest accounts lost at JFIM.

Jardine Fleming, a joint venture between private British bank Robert Fleming and Jardine Matheson, last August revealed a five-month probe by British and Hong Kong regulators into irregular trades by a former senior fund manager at JFIM.
